newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CLIFFORD SEES YR NET OVER A$13.4 MLN.
newsitem.headline: CLIFFORD SEES YR NET OVER A$13.4 MLN.

text.p: Bus manufacturer Clifford Corp said on Monday it expected to achieve earnings before interest and tax including abnormals of more than A$15.4 million for the year to June 30, 1997.

Clifford chairman Barrie Loiterton said net profit after interest should exceed A$13.4 million and turnover would be more than A$80 million. The group is due to announce its results in around two weeks, Loiterton told an extraordinary general meeting called to approve a June share placement.
The company was confident of reaching its turnover target of A$129 million in the current year to June 30, 1998, he said.
Loiterton said directors were expected to recommend a final dividend of at least 2.25 cents a share to add to the 1.25 cent a share interim dividend.
Clifford, a former mining company which turned to bus manufacturing through acquisitions last year, reported an interim net profit of A$8.41 million.
Its 1995/96 net profit was A$3.00 million.
Loiterton said Clifford remained confident of winning a substantial part of the New South Wales State Transit Authority's so-called Olympic contract to supply 300 to 600 buses.
He said delays in letting the contract, expected in June, were apparently due to NSW government funding decisions.
